raw_response:
I’m 50 this year, never spent a day in school. My father taught me to farm, and I’ve been doing it for 30 years. Our land is 10.9 mu, all flat, good soil but not the richest. There are six of us under the roof, but my son and his wife work at the textile factory in town, and my old mother can’t get out to the fields anymore. So it’s mostly me and my wife handling the crops. We don’t have much cash sitting around after my daughter got married last spring, so I have to be careful with every yuan I spend.

We do wheat and maize double crop, same as every family around here. For wheat, I always plant around October 10th to 15th, depending on when the autumn rain comes. If the ground is too dry, I wait a few more days. This year I’ll use mostly my own saved seed — I kept about 600 jin of wheat from last harvest. It’s a local white-grain variety that does fine. I’ll buy maybe two small bags of new seed just in case, because saved seed can get sick. That keeps the seed cost down.

For fertilizer, I’d like to put more, but I can only afford about ten big bags of urea for the whole year, plus two bags of that compound fertilizer (the one with the three numbers). I’ll spread most of the compound stuff and about half a bag of urea per mu before sowing wheat. Then in March, when the wheat wakes up, if it looks yellow I’ll topdress another quarter bag per mu. I know some neighbors use more, but I can’t borrow money for fertilizer. Better to have some cash left for my mother’s medicine.

Irrigation costs money because the well electricity is metered now. I’ll water wheat three times: once right after planting if it doesn’t rain, once at jointing in April, and once at heading in May. I’d like to water a fourth time, but the electric bill last year was too high. For maize, if July rains are good I might not water at all, but usually I give it one good watering when the ears are forming — that’s enough if the season isn’t too dry.

For maize, we plant as soon as the wheat is off the field — usually June 12th to 15th. There’s no time to rest. I hire the tractor to chop the wheat straw and do a quick rotary till, then we plant the same day or next. I always buy hybrid maize seed, new bags every year. Saved maize seed is no good, everyone knows that. I put about half a bag of urea per mu in the hole at planting. That’s all the fertilizer maize gets — no money for more.

Pesticides: for wheat I spray herbicide once in early spring, and keep an eye out for aphids. If they show up, I’ll spray insecticide. For maize, I put down pre-emergent herbicide right after planting, and that’s usually enough. I don’t spray maize insecticide unless the worms get really bad, because that chemical is expensive.

Labor: me and my wife do almost everything. I’ll hire two day-laborers for the wheat planting rush and maybe one day for the maize harvest if the weather looks bad and we need to get it in quick. Hired help is 120 yuan a day now, which hurts.

I expect about seven or eight hundred jin per mu of wheat and maybe nine hundred jin per mu of maize. Last year we got a little more, but you can’t count on that. I’d rather be a bit low and be happy than count on a big crop and be disappointed.
